newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok Bank sees slower 1996 earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok Bank sees slower 1996 earnings growth.

text.p: Thailand's biggest bank, Bangkok Bank, expects earnings growth for calendar 1996 to be around eight percent against 13 percent growth in 1995, a senior executive said on Wednesday.

Satit Uthaisri, group executive vice-president, told Reuters that earnings growth for the Thai banking sector in general would be lower this year in line with a slowing economy. But overall performance would not be as bad as some might anticipate, he added.
Bangkok Bank's consolidated earnings in 1995 rose to 19.88 billion baht ($788 million) or 19.86 baht per share from 17.45 billion or 17.45 baht in 1994.
"That (bank's earnings growth projection) is still considered satisfactory. The car can't run at full speed all the time...now we have to slow down," he said.

His comments came as foreign investors sold mainly bank stocks on the Thai bourse on the belief that restrictive foreign loan importation measures announced by the central bank would hurt the sector's business.
Expectations that Bangkok Bank would raise its interest on fixed deposits by 25 basis points and that other banks would follow also dampened sentiment on the bourse, brokers said.
But Satit said the slowdown in the Thai economy, hit by sagging exports and a widening current account deficit, would show a clearer impact on the banking sector next year rather than this year.
"The banking sector will not slow down ahead of other sectors. If there will be any visible impact at all, it should be next year. This year will still be all right," he said.
